I live in Los Angeles and have gone carless for most of 2014. Well, I guess I have gone about 90% carless for all of 2014.  Before thatid say I was about 50% car dependent through 2013. It takes some planning and some tough choices and some getting used to, but I think it's no different than the planning, tough choices, and getting used to it takes to drive a car everywhere. It's just that those decisions have been taken for granted as just part of living in the big city, so it makes the thought of ditching your car seem a lot harder than it actual is. The hardest is to really just wrap your head around it and decide to do it. 

For a very long time a car has been a symbol of freedom in America, but with the cost of maintenance, the need for insurance, the availability of parking, the constraints of traffic, etc. that freedom is in actuality less and less a reality.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Hanabi's pretty cool - it's a co-operative game where you have to collectively play cards in order from 1 to 5 in each of five colours. You get three "lives" so you can't make many mistakes. The difficulty is in that you are not allowed to see your own cards, and can only communicate with others about their cards with limited information, e.g. "Those three cards are red," or "you have no fours". It's really hard, but interesting.

Having played both Dominion and Ascension a fair bit against AI on my phone, I can say that Dominion has much less theme, but less swinginess since the cards you can buy are in 10 piles of 10 rather than an ever-shifting central row, and there's only one kind of currency. I like both, but I think Dominion is the better game - many people disagree with me though!

Having played both Dominion and Ascension a fair bit against AI on my phone, I can say that Dominion has much less theme, but less swinginess since the cards you can buy are in 10 piles of 10 rather than an ever-shifting central row, and there's only one kind of currency. I know this is off-topic, but I had to poke my head in here, as Dominion was my addiction just before Sentinels (though I still have three expansions of Dominion to acquire…in time) - I agree completely that Dominion is a better game, primarily because there are more options for strategy and more chances for player interaction.  Also it feels better paced unless you have more than four people playing.

If you want to try something that is very themed but has more deckbuilding options than Ascension offers, you might try Thunderstone.  It has little in the way of player interaction, unfortunately, but I found the game mechanics (darkness penalties, physical vs. magic attack, heroes, weapons, items, spells, villagers, and some more) to be more interesting in Thunderstone.  It does tend to be a bit slower than other deckbuilders though.
